events.title: Congress Adopts the Stars and Stripes
events.description: The Second Continental Congress passed a resolution establishing the flag of the United States. It called for thirteen stripes and thirteen stars, one for each of the original states.
events.significance: The design became a lasting national symbol. The anniversary is now observed as Flag Day in the United States, which President Woodrow Wilson proclaimed in 1916.

events.title: Birth of Che Guevara
events.description: Ernesto Guevara de la Serna was born in Rosario, Argentina. He trained as a doctor before becoming a revolutionary and a key figure in the Cuban Revolution.
events.significance: Guevara became one of the best-known and most debated figures of the 20th century. His image is a worldwide emblem of rebellion.

events.title: German Troops Enter Paris
events.description: German forces occupied the French capital during World War II. The French government had left days earlier, and about a million residents fled the city.
events.significance: The fall of Paris marked a turning point in the Battle of France. It began a four-year occupation that ended only with the city's liberation in 1944.

events.title: Death of Jorge Luis Borges
events.description: The Argentine writer died of liver cancer in Geneva, Switzerland, at age 86. He was known for poems, essays and short stories such as those in Ficciones.
events.significance: Borges' work on labyrinths, infinity and imagination shaped modern literature. It influenced writers around the world.
